claim: The created file record is not associated with the `userId`, allowing any authenticated user with `jobs:read` scope to retrieve another user's file by ID.
reason: HANDOFF §7 + SPEC §2 notes: File has no userId column, ownership is path-based (cockpitUserDir, files.ts:8; resolveCockpitFile). No endpoint serves a File by id: the file route looks up by packageId with userId in the where (api/cockpit/files/[packageId]/route.ts:37-44)

claim: No reference to COCKPIT_SCOPES, jobs:read, package:write, or any scope defaults - AC-10 requires new MCP tokens to receive five-element default scopes via spread from COCKPIT_SCOPES
reason: Scopes are assigned in createMcpToken (mcpToken.actions.ts:47-52), not in generateToken; AC-10 is satisfied there

claim: Return type lacks scopes field required by AC-10 for new MCP tokens with five default scopes
reason: generateToken only makes the secret; scopes are stored by createMcpToken (mcpToken.actions.ts:47-52)

claim: The originOf function only validates that protocol is http: or https:, but doesn't validate the host. A malicious GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI could have a valid http/https protocol but point to an attacker-controlled domain, allowing open redirects.
reason: GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI is operator-set env, not attacker input; originOf only decides which origin our own redirects use (SPEC §6.2 'Origin')

claim: The function returns null when missingGmailEnv().length > 0, but the type signature says GoogleConfig | null. When it returns null due to missing env vars, the caller may not handle this case. Also, the origin is cast as string with 'as string' even though originOf can return null, which could lead
reason: missingGmailEnv() adds GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI when originOf is null (oauth.ts:86), so getGoogleConfig returns null before the `as string` cast (:97)

claim: The unique constraint on (userId, idempotencyKey) should also include status to prevent idempotency key reuse across different states, but current implementation allows same idempotency key after package transitions through states like 'rejected' -> 'pending'
reason: Replay of the same key returns the existing package (SPEC §2.2 step 2); unique(userId, idempotencyKey) deliberately ignores status

claim: Two non-atomic fields for send lock mechanism with no transaction boundary enforcement. Process death between setting sendStartedAt and writing sendOutcome can leave package in limbo
reason: SPEC §6.4 stale-lock rule covers a crash between lock and outcome: panel after 60 s (send.ts:267-278, SendOutcomePanel.tsx:37-47)

claim: Multiple manual edit fields (changeRequest, editedAt, etc.) without timestamp coordination. Concurrent edits to fitAnalysis, letterMd, cvJson can cause lost updates
reason: HANDOFF §7: edits have no optimistic-concurrency check (last write wins; Send re-checks updatedAt)

claim: Gmail badge lacks aria-label like fitGrade badge has, missing ARIA attribute for accessibility
reason: Accessibility/UX nit; the control has visible text and no SPEC AC requires the suggested change

claim: Server is created/connected/closed per request in stateless mode, but transport state (including any pending async writes) may persist if handleRequest throws between connect and close. Server.close() is not in a finally block.
reason: Upstream request pattern; McpServer is created per request and holds no timers, handleRequest returns error responses instead of throwing. Cosmetic (could wrap in try/finally)

claim: Open redirect / XSS risk: jobUrl is user-controlled data from pkg.job.jobUrl and rendered without sanitization. formatUrl may not properly validate the URL scheme.
reason: formatUrl prefixes anything not starting with http:// or https:// with https:// (utils.ts:32-37), so javascript:/data: cannot form a scheme

claim: The action is called with pkg.id without verifying the userId in the session owns this package. The response message could leak information about other users' data through error messages.
reason: Ownership is checked server-side (packages.ts:384,211); another user's id gives NOT_FOUND with a fixed message (errors.ts:11), no enumeration signal beyond 'Not found'

claim: userId is extracted from ctx for scope checks and rate limiting, but the run callback receives only the parsed input (T), not ctx or userId. The data-access functions (submitPackage, markChangeRequestDone, attachFile) are invoked inside run and therefore cannot scope their DB queries by userId from
reason: userId is closed over from ctx in registerCockpitTools (cockpit.ts:94) and passed explicitly: attachFile(userId,..) :102, submitPackage(userId,..) :118, markChangeRequestDone(userId,..) :293

claim: If GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI is missing/unparseable, redirects become relative which could violate AC-22 'redirects relative to the origin'
reason: Relative Location is the documented fallback when no usable origin exists (oauth.ts:104); same-origin relative redirect is not an open redirect, and getGoogleConfig fails first with not_configured

claim: No database-level state machine enforcement; any status transition is allowed via raw SQL or buggy app code.
reason: 'sending' is not a status; the lock is sendStartedAt and the 60 s stale rule recovers a crash (send.ts:267-278)

claim: idempotencyKey is nullable; SQLite allows multiple NULLs in a unique index, so duplicate NULL keys bypass deduplication.
reason: SPEC §2 notes / D-005 D8: nullable idempotencyKey, any number of keyless packages is intended

claim: Email recipient displayed to user could expose sensitive email addresses or be used for phishing if emailTo contains attacker-controlled data
reason: Showing the recipient to the user is the feature; the Send dialog adds the domain warning (SendDialog.tsx:58-78)

claim: The shard does not implement five panels as required by AC-18; only 2 panels (Posting, CV) are visible
reason: Panels.tsx exports Posting/Cv/Fit/Email/Letter panels (:58,89,150,187,212) and DetailView renders all five (DetailView.tsx:134-141)

claim: AC-18 requires a letter panel but no letter panel component exists despite import of renderLetterMarkdown
reason: LetterPanel exists at Panels.tsx:212 and uses renderLetterMarkdown

claim: AC-24 requires CRLF throughout and correct headers. The function validates headers but only calls header() for validation - the values are not validated for non-empty content (only checked at line 69 for from/to).
reason: mime.ts:24-29 header() throws on CR/LF for From/To/Subject/attachment name, mime.ts:66 enforces printable ASCII without quotes, schemas.ts:7-23 reject CR/LF in emailTo/emailSubject, body and PDF are base64 (mime.ts:90,96)

claim: Missing 'use client' directive - component uses client-only hooks (useState, useEffect, useMemo, useRouter) but is not declared as client component
reason: EditForm.tsx line 1 is "use client"

claim: getGmailSettings returns account data from AC-43 compliant select (email, scopes only) but is missing revalidatePath call for consistency with data modification patterns.
reason: A read action needs no revalidatePath

claim: Primary CTA 'Approve' has no aria-label or visible text that clearly indicates the action for screen reader users on focused button
reason: Accessibility/UX nit; the control has visible text and no SPEC AC requires the suggested change

claim: Sticky footer region at bottom of 375px screen may cause content truncation issues and hard-to-reach target for thumb interaction on mobile
reason: Sticky bar is the SPEC §5.3 design ('sticky at the bottom on mobile'); H-check AC-20, not a code defect

claim: CR/LF header injection protection exists for emailTo but may be incomplete - need to verify emailSubject and other fields are also protected to prevent MIME injection
reason: mime.ts:24-29 header() throws on CR/LF for From/To/Subject/attachment name, mime.ts:66 enforces printable ASCII without quotes, schemas.ts:7-23 reject CR/LF in emailTo/emailSubject, body and PDF are base64 (mime.ts:90,96)

claim: Cannot verify if updatePackageContent action checks userId from session before operating on packages - this IS CRITICAL for authorization
reason: updatePackageContent -> reload(userId,id) and transition() with userId (packages.ts:229-235, 384, 402)

claim: Violates AC-34 by modifying a locked package (clearing sendStartedAt and sendOutcome), contradicting the 'frozen' requirement for packages with sendStartedAt set
reason: SPEC §6.4 'Recovery actions' explicitly act on a locked approved package (recoverable(), send.ts:267-278); AC-34 freezes every other transition, not these two

claim: sendOutcome set to null on success, but AC-33 states it should be cleared (set to null). However, if Gmail call times out (AC-33), sendOutcome='unknown' is set. On success, sending null is correct per AC-33, but there's inconsistency: success path clears it via update, while timeout path sets it to
reason: SPEC §6.4 step 6 / stale-lock rule: crash or failed record step leaves lock + unknown outcome, recovered via markSendUnknownAsSent (send.ts:249-257,290-309). Finding itself concludes this is by design

claim: AC-23 requires checking state before ?error= parameter is checked. The code throws 'invalid_state' before checking params.get('error'), but this means the ?error= check happens after state validation - which matches 'checked before ?error='.
reason: Not a defect: finding concludes the code matches AC-23 (state checked before ?error=, callback/route.ts:81-86)

claim: AC-23 requires rejecting a userId mismatch - code validates that cookie.userId matches session userId
reason: Not a defect: finding concludes the code matches AC-23 (session_mismatch, :84)

claim: AC-23 requires rejecting a missing refresh_token - code checks for refreshToken and throws 'no_refresh_token'
reason: Not a defect: no_refresh_token is thrown at :94

claim: AC-23 requires rejecting id_token with wrong aud/iss/exp/nonce and unverified email. verifyIdToken handles aud/iss/exp/nonce validation, assertScopeAndAddress should handle scope and email verification. Need to verify what assertScopeAndAddress checks.
reason: verifyIdToken checks aud/iss/exp/nonce/email_verified (oauth.ts:188-222) and assertScopeAndAddress checks scope + allow-list (:224-235)

claim: AC-23 requires deleting the cookie on every exit - finish() function sets maxAge: 0 which deletes the cookie
reason: Not a defect: every exit goes through finish() which expires the cookie (:38-44)

claim: AC-16 requires 401 for no session, 404 for file outside cockpit dir, missing package, or auth failure - but error handling does not distinguish these cases
reason: AC-16 (401/404) concerns the file route; this page maps NOT_FOUND to notFound() and UNAUTHENTICATED to /signin (page.tsx:22-24)

claim: Missing auth scope validation on handleSaveMatchResultsBatch tool
reason: save_match_results_batch checks jobs:write at route.ts:220; no deleteJob tool exists

claim: AC-18 states the detail page shows five panels (posting, CV, fit analysis, email preview with attachment size, letter). The imports include PostingPanel, CvPanel, FitPanel, EmailPanel, LetterPanel, and PreviousReviewInfo - a six-panel import that appears to include an extra panel not specified in AC
reason: PreviousReviewInfo is required by SPEC §5.3 'Previous review info'; the five-panel AC-18 count does not exclude it

claim: Tag model has no max constraints on label or value fields and no index on createdBy for access pattern. Unique constraint is correctly scoped by createdBy. However, potential for tag spam with unlimited tags per user not enforced at schema level.
reason: Upstream Tag model, untouched by cockpit

claim: No userId validation or scoping in list jobs schema - relies on handler to scope queries to current user
reason: A zod schema holds no query; list_jobs builds the where with userId (mcp/tools/cockpit.ts:136)

claim: The row.id is used directly as React key without validation. If row.id is predictable or exposed, it could enable Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR) if QueueRow doesn't properly enforce user-scoped access to row data.
reason: React key only; rows are already user-scoped by listPackagesByTab (packages.ts:416)

claim: Cannot verify data source security from this shard. Per AC-14, need to confirm data is user-scoped and userId is validated before query execution. The `getReviewQueue` action must enforce user scoping.
reason: getReviewQueue -> listPackagesByTab(userId,..) with userId in the where (packages.ts:414-416)

claim: Without seeing the full disconnectGmail action and how user context is obtained, cannot verify if user is taken from session before performing DB operations
reason: disconnectGmail calls requireUser() first (cockpitGmail.actions.ts:43) and deletes only user.id's row (:58)

claim: cvFileId references a file but schema doesn't define foreign key behavior - critical for cascade deletes and orphaned file handling
reason: cvFile relation is onDelete: SetNull (SPEC §2); orphan files are an accepted V0 follow-up (SPEC §3 'Unreferenced files are not cleaned up')

claim: AC-15 requires `updatePackageContent` validates idempotentKey and rejects terminal statuses/locked packages, but this `submitInTransaction` function lacks check for terminal statuses (sent, superseded, rejected) when using idempotency key replay. The replay should verify the existing package isn't i
reason: SPEC §2.2 step 2: an idempotent replay returns the existing package unchanged whatever its status; AC-15 is about updatePackageContent, not submit

claim: AC-15 requires refusing terminal statuses. This checks only 'sent' status but misses other terminal statuses: 'superseded' or 'rejected' - these could allow subsequent submits which violates SPEC.
reason: A rejected active package is blocked at step 4 (packages.ts:112-117 JOB_REJECTED); superseded packages are by design replaced by a new version

claim: Package ID comes from component props which are typically passed via URL params without extracting and validating user from session/token first
reason: Authorization is server-side per action (cockpit.actions.ts:40, packages.ts:211)

claim: The scoped entry contains ONLY X-Frame-Options, but the SPEC requires the global /(.*) entry to have X-Content-Type-Options AND X-Frame-Options, and the scoped entry should have ONLY X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN
reason: next.config.mjs:6-20 is exactly AC-37: global entry first, then a scoped entry with only X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN. The global entry's nosniff is upstream and AC-37 only constrains the scoped entry

claim: The component receives packageId as a prop with no verification that the current user owns this package. A stolen MCP token with jobs:read scope could pass any packageId and call these actions.
reason: Actions are server-authorized: markSendUnknownAsSent/releaseSendLock where includes userId (send.ts:267-272)

claim: No authorization check is performed at the batch level. Each job in the batch is processed sequentially without verifying that the caller has permission to add jobs. With jobs:read scope, the token should not be able to write at all.
reason: Upstream tool, not modified by cockpit (git log shows only pre-cockpit commits); out of cockpit scope, and AC-46/49/50 govern cockpit tools only; scope jobs:write is checked in route.ts:197

claim: This function performs a WRITE operation (UPDATE) on a resume without validating that the MCP token has 'resume:write' or equivalent scope. A token with only 'jobs:read' scope should not be able to modify resume data.
reason: Upstream tool, not modified by cockpit (git log shows only pre-cockpit commits); out of cockpit scope, and AC-46/49/50 govern cockpit tools only; no-scope design noted at route.ts:238-242

claim: Package ID is taken from user input but NOT validated against ownership before being passed to service functions. The `id` parameter flows to `approvePackageSvc` without any prior ownership check.
reason: Ownership is enforced inside the service: transition() where carries userId (packages.ts:211-218). 'Attack surface' is not a bug; the claim's 'stolen MCP token' cannot call server actions (session only)

claim: Error code is exposed in redirect URL without sanitization, allowing open redirect vulnerability
reason: Error `code` is a closed enum (OAuthError.code or the literal token_exchange_failed, :149) and Location is built from the env origin (redirectLocation, oauth.ts:105-108); no user input reaches the URL

claim: Version number allocation is not atomic under concurrent submits - could create duplicate versions
reason: Writes are conditional updateMany (packages.ts:211-219) and unique indexes backstop version/idempotency races (P2002 -> CONFLICT, packages.ts:69-81; SPEC §2.2 Concurrency)

claim: updateMany + findFirst pattern is not atomic - TOCTOU race between update success check and subsequent operations
reason: The state change is the single conditional updateMany (packages.ts:211-219); the findFirst only classifies a count of 0 as NOT_FOUND vs INVALID_STATE (:221-226). No later step assumes it won

claim: AC-50 requires: 'A denied call returns `isError: true` with `RATE_LIMITED`'
reason: Upstream tool, not modified by cockpit (git log shows only pre-cockpit commits); out of cockpit scope, and AC-46/49/50 govern cockpit tools only

claim: save_match_result requires 'jobs:write' but should likely require 'matches:write' based on resource type
reason: There is no matches:write scope in the system; save_match_result uses jobs:write by upstream design

claim: review_resume scope check comment on lines 238-242 states intentionally no scope gate, but this contradicts security principle of authenticating all tool access
reason: Upstream decision documented in route.ts:238-242 (tokens predating resume:write must keep working); SPEC §3 says cockpit tools do not copy it

claim: The userId parameter is accepted but the rate limit check result is not awaited, creating a timing issue and potential race condition. The function calls checkMcpRateLimit(userId) synchronously but doesn't await it - if checkMcpRateLimit returns a Promise, this will fail silently or cause unexpected
reason: Upstream tool, not modified by cockpit (git log shows only pre-cockpit commits); out of cockpit scope, and AC-46/49/50 govern cockpit tools only; checkMcpRateLimit is synchronous (rate-limit.ts:22-54)

claim: The idempotency key replay only checks jobId match, not status. Same key with different jobId is rejected, but same key with same jobId in any state (including 'sent') returns the package.
reason: Same key + same job returns the existing package by SPEC §2.2 step 2; same key + other job throws CONFLICT (packages.ts:57, D-008). Claim contradicts itself

claim: Rate limit denial should return `isError: true` with `RATE_LIMITED` code per AC-50
reason: Upstream tool, not modified by cockpit (git log shows only pre-cockpit commits); out of cockpit scope, and AC-46/49/50 govern cockpit tools only

claim: userId is accepted as parameter without verifying it matches the authenticated session - missing auth boundary check before any processing
reason: Upstream tool, not modified by cockpit (git log shows only pre-cockpit commits); out of cockpit scope, and AC-46/49/50 govern cockpit tools only; Handlers/services are only called with the userId from the session/token (cockpit.actions.ts:40, mcp/route.ts:58,272); there is no caller-supplied userId path

claim: Import from cockpit/schemas is empty barrelling - need to verify this type is not accessible to users and whether schemas are validated at runtime
reason: updatePackageContent re-parses with UpdatePackageContentSchema in the service (packages.ts:383); type-only import has no runtime role

claim: The function iterates over `input.results` array without validating the size of the batch. An attacker could provide an extremely large array causing DoS via memory exhaustion or processing time.
reason: Upstream tool, not modified by cockpit (git log shows only pre-cockpit commits); out of cockpit scope, and AC-46/49/50 govern cockpit tools only; the schema caps the array at MCP_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS (mcp.schema.ts:225-235)

claim: Non-400/401/403 errors for 'send' kind are not explicitly handled, potentially missing other definitive Gmail API errors that could indicate message delivery state
reason: For kind 'send' any non-2xx becomes GMAIL_SEND with definitive only for 400/401/403 (client.ts:68-75); 404/5xx are ambiguous by SPEC §6.4. The claim 'falls through to GMAIL_TOKEN' is false

claim: The client directive is correct, but we cannot verify AC-28 coverage that only `sendPackage` server action calls `sendApplicationPackage` without examining the imported file.
reason: AC-28 is checked by grep/AC-35 test; sendPackage calls sendApplicationPackage directly (cockpitSend.actions.ts:59)

claim: Need to verify that type PackageDetail and formatBytes utility don't transitively import server-only modules or expose server secrets.
reason: Panels.tsx imports only a type from the actions module (Panels.tsx:14) and formatBytes is local; neither pulls server code into the client bundle

claim: SQLite migrations are DDL-compatible by design - Prisma migrate generates raw SQL DDL. Migration should be pure DDL.
reason: Not a finding: the migration is 8 CREATE statements and no ALTER/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP (migration.sql; __tests__/cockpit/migration.spec.ts exists for AC-01)

claim: The where-clause includes `status: "approved"` but NOT `sendOutcome: null`, allowing this lock-clearing operation to run on a package that already has `sendOutcome: "unknown"`. According to AC-33, only locked packages with unresolved outcome should have `markSendUnknownAsSent` called, but this funct
reason: releaseQuietly runs only for the call that just took the lock and failed definitively before/at Gmail (send.ts:191-196, 203-206); sendOutcome is still null then. The only overlap needs a send in flight >60 s (bounded by 2x20 s timeouts)

claim: The scope set that is spread into the DEFAULT token scopes bundles a data-mutating scope (package:write) together with the read scope (jobs:read). Any token minted from the defaults therefore carries write access to packages, so the 'read-only MCP client' posture (jobs:read) that the rest of the sys
reason: D-007 N9 ruling: COCKPIT_SCOPES is spread into default token scopes always; HANDOFF §3 recommends a dedicated bot token

claim: The email comparison uses toLowerCase() on both sides, which is correct for case-insensitive email comparison as per RFC 5321. The allowedAddress is trimmed to handle potential whitespace. However, the scope parsing uses .split(/\s+/) which could be exploited with unusual whitespace characters (tabs
reason: Google returns a space-separated scope string; split(/\s+/).includes(GMAIL_SEND_SCOPE) handles any whitespace run; email compare is lowercase on both sides (oauth.ts:232)

claim: The function receives userId parameter but there's no guarantee that getPackageWithJob actually scopes the query by userId. If the underlying implementation allows querying any package by id regardless of ownership, user B could access user A's package/cvFile.
reason: getPackageWithJob uses findFirst({ id, userId }) (packages.ts:441-443) and throws NOT_FOUND

claim: No transaction or atomic operation around status transitions. Double-click or concurrent approval/rejection can cause inconsistent state
reason: Writes are conditional updateMany (packages.ts:211-219) and unique indexes backstop version/idempotency races (P2002 -> CONFLICT, packages.ts:69-81; SPEC §2.2 Concurrency); a double approve: second updateMany matches 0 rows -> INVALID_STATE

claim: Version number is application-managed, not database-enforced, creating race condition under concurrent package creation
reason: Writes are conditional updateMany (packages.ts:211-219) and unique indexes backstop version/idempotency races (P2002 -> CONFLICT, packages.ts:69-81; SPEC §2.2 Concurrency)

claim: sentVia field creates two different code paths (gmail vs manual) with different state effects but no validation or enforcement. Status transition logic may differ
reason: sentVia is set by the two code paths that own it (send.ts:227, packages.ts:327, send.ts:298); nothing else writes status 'sent'

claim: The in‑memory `store` can grow without bound because cleanup only runs when `store.size` exceeds `CLEANUP_THRESHOLD` and only removes entries whose `resetTime` has passed. An attacker can flood the server with many distinct `userId` values to exhaust memory.
reason: Keys are userId(+bucket) of authenticated token holders only (cockpit.ts:71-74), so cardinality equals the number of users; entries expire and are swept past 500 (rate-limit.ts:35-39)

claim: Returns a text message instead of error object per AC-50
reason: Upstream tool, not modified by cockpit (git log shows only pre-cockpit commits); out of cockpit scope, and AC-46/49/50 govern cockpit tools only

claim: Gmail chip shows when Gmail is disconnected, but SPEC AC-47 requires: 'the Gmail callout appears when Gmail is disconnected and an approved package with emailTo exists'
reason: D-006 spec choice (c): the Gmail chip means 'package has an emailTo and Gmail is not connected'; the AC-47 callout is a separate element (QueueView.tsx:44-59, queue gmailCalloutNeeded)

claim: Package action (approvePackage) is called with only pkg.id from the detail passed as prop, with no explicit userId verification or scoping. The user could potentially approve a package they shouldn't have access to.
reason: Authorization is server-side (packages.ts:249-253, transition where userId)

claim: Unapprove action receives only pkg.id without explicit userId scoping, same vulnerability as SEC-001.
reason: Authorization is server-side (packages.ts:256-262)

claim: The function trusts the `userId` argument without verifying it comes from the authenticated session or token.
reason: Upstream tool, not modified by cockpit (git log shows only pre-cockpit commits); out of cockpit scope, and AC-46/49/50 govern cockpit tools only; Handlers/services are only called with the userId from the session/token (cockpit.actions.ts:40, mcp/route.ts:58,272); there is no caller-supplied userId path

claim: The WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport is imported but never used in the provided shard (lines 1-178). The entire file snippet doesn't show it being instantiated or used.
reason: The transport import is used at route.ts:275

claim: okResult serializes arbitrary data returned by run() directly into the tool result with no redaction, field allowlist, or size limit. If run returns objects containing tokens, internal file paths, PII from other users' jobs, or sensitive configuration, that data is exposed to the MCP client. An atta
reason: submit returns only {packageId, version, status, supersededIds, idempotent} (cockpit.ts:119-125); get_job returns the token owner's own rows (cockpit.ts:194-230)

claim: Default redirect URI uses http://localhost:3737 which lacks Secure cookie flag, creating mixed security posture
reason: SPEC §6.2 / AC-22: Secure iff the redirect URI is https; the http localhost default is intentional (cfg.secure, oauth.ts:98)

claim: The packageId is taken directly from URL params without being validated against the authenticated user first, before DB operations occur.
reason: getPackageDetail -> getPackageWithJob findFirst({ id, userId }) (packages.ts:441-443); another user's id gives NOT_FOUND -> notFound() (page.tsx:23-24)

claim: Missing session authentication guard at page level - relies entirely on actions to authenticate, but no early return if session invalid before any processing.
reason: SPEC §1 P5 design: requireUser() runs first inside every action (cockpit.actions.ts:40) before any DB access; page maps UNAUTHENTICATED to redirect (page.tsx:22)

claim: The page forwards the raw `account` object returned by `getGmailSettings` to the client‑side `GmailCard` component, which can expose sensitive fields such as `encryptedRefreshToken` or `iv`, violating SPEC AC‑43 that the Gmail account must never reach the client.
reason: getGmailSettings selects only { email, scopes } (cockpitGmail.actions.ts:29-32); encryptedRefreshToken/iv are never loaded for this page

claim: sendStartedAt acts as a lock but has no TTL enforcement; stale lock recovery is purely application-dependent.
reason: SPEC §6.4 'Stale lock': enforced in application code by design (recoverable(), send.ts:267-278)

claim: Version allocation race: two concurrent creators read MAX(version), both compute +1, one fails on unique index — but the loser has no clear retry path.
reason: Writes are conditional updateMany (packages.ts:211-219) and unique indexes backstop version/idempotency races (P2002 -> CONFLICT, packages.ts:69-81; SPEC §2.2 Concurrency); CONFLICT means the caller replays (D-005 D7)

claim: The token creation hardcodes `jobs:write` in the scopes array, but AC-10 specifies that new MCP tokens should get `jobs:read` among the three existing defaults plus `jobs:read` and `package:write`.
reason: Defaults are jobs:write, questions:write, resume:write + COCKPIT_SCOPES (= jobs:read, package:write) (mcpToken.actions.ts:47-52) = AC-10's five scopes

claim: The function performs database operations (requireUser count check, token creation) without first validating that the token/scopes meet required criteria, violating AC-09 which mandates scope rejection before any DB access.
reason: AC-09 scope-before-DB applies to cockpit MCP tools (cockpit.ts:69), not to token creation, which requires a session (requireUser first)

claim: The email fields (to, subject, body) are passed directly to MIME construction without visible header injection sanitization. The spec mentions CR/LF header injection concerns.
reason: mime.ts:24-29 header() throws on CR/LF for From/To/Subject/attachment name, mime.ts:66 enforces printable ASCII without quotes, schemas.ts:7-23 reject CR/LF in emailTo/emailSubject, body and PDF are base64 (mime.ts:90,96)

claim: row.emailTo is displayed directly without sanitization - could contain malicious content from attacker-controlled job posting
reason: emailTo is rendered as a React text node (QueueRow.tsx:68), so markup is escaped; schema also restricts it to a single email address

claim: Interview model lacks userId or createdBy field, allowing potential cross-user data access
reason: Upstream Interview model, untouched by cockpit

claim: Boundary and messageId use randomBytes/randomUUID but attachment name is interpolated directly into Content-Disposition header at line 92-93 without CR/LF validation
reason: mime.ts:24-29 header() throws on CR/LF for From/To/Subject/attachment name, mime.ts:66 enforces printable ASCII without quotes, schemas.ts:7-23 reject CR/LF in emailTo/emailSubject, body and PDF are base64 (mime.ts:90,96); attachment name is checked at mime.ts:63 before interpolation at :92-93

claim: Server action imported to component without explicit 'use client' guard - boundary clarity depends on file location and action export design
reason: "use client" is present (EditForm.tsx:1); importing a server action from a client component is the normal Next pattern

claim: The catch block silently swallows all exceptions during token revocation, which could mask non-recoverable errors like invalid ciphertext or malformed tokens.
reason: Best-effort revoke is the SPEC §6.2 ruling: a lost key or dead token must not block deleting the row (cockpitGmail.actions.ts:54-56)

claim: revalidatePath uses root segment pattern without dynamic route handling; paths may not cover all affected routes including potential dynamic folders.

claim: Token hashing uses a single pass of SHA-256 with no keying or salting, making offline brute-attack on a token database computationally cheaper compared to a keyed hash like HKDF or PBKDF2/Argon2.
reason: Upstream tool, not modified by cockpit (git log shows only pre-cockpit commits); out of cockpit scope, and AC-46/49/50 govern cockpit tools only
